facts.title: Canada — official languages
facts.text: English and French are Canada’s two official languages.

facts.title: Sir John A. Macdonald — first prime minister
facts.text: Sir John A. Macdonald became Canada’s first prime minister in 1867.

facts.title: Canadian Constitution — 1982 patriation
facts.text: Canada’s Constitution was patriated from the United Kingdom in 1982.

facts.title: Costa Rica — abolition of permanent army
facts.text: Costa Rica’s 1949 Constitution outlawed the army as a permanent institution.

facts.title: South America — twelve sovereign states
facts.text: South America contains 12 sovereign states; this source-page reference excludes French Guiana, which is not a sovereign state.

facts.title: Isthmus of Panama — continental link
facts.text: The Isthmus of Panama connects North and South America; the Panama Canal traverses part of the isthmus.

facts.title: Brazil — South American area comparison
facts.text: Brazil is the largest country in South America by area.

facts.title: Brazil — 1822 independence
facts.text: The source records Brazil’s independence from Portugal in 1822; this is preserved as a historical reference.

facts.title: Brasília — capital of Brazil
facts.text: Brasília is the capital of Brazil.

facts.title: Buenos Aires — Río de la Plata
facts.text: Buenos Aires is located on the Río de la Plata estuary.

facts.title: Ecuador — name and equator
facts.text: The name Ecuador derives from the Spanish word for the equator.

facts.title: Galápagos — Darwin historical context
facts.text: Charles Darwin’s work on evolution is historically associated with observations in the Galápagos Islands.

facts.title: Dilma Rousseff — historic first
facts.text: Dilma Rousseff became Brazil’s first female elected president in 2010.
